subject: Demo recap + proposed POC plan — FinServCorp
messages:
From: Dylan Brooks <dylan@redwoodinference.com>
To: Maya Singh <maya@finservcorp.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwoodinference.com>, Neha Kapoor <neha_kapoor@redwoodinference.com>
Date: 2027-05-02T14:10:00-07:00
Subject: Demo recap + proposed POC plan — FinServCorp

Hi Maya / Raj,

Thanks again for taking the demo with us earlier today — great discussion. Below is a short recap and a proposed POC plan to validate Redwood Inference for your customer-facing insights pipeline. I attached a one-page POC plan and an evaluation metrics template for your team to review.

Quick recap:
- Scope: Real-time extraction + summarization pipeline for customer support chats (English).
- Current concern: inconsistent latency during peak hours and difficulty keeping unit cost within budget while maintaining response quality.
- Demo highlights: model variants that meet accuracy targets, auto-batching to reduce cost, and routing/fallback behavior for availability.

Proposed POC (6 weeks) — high level:
1) Success criteria (what success looks like):
   - Latency: p95 inference latency < 500ms for 2k concurrent reqs (typical 1-2s token lengths)
   - Cost: per-1k-token cost reduction >= 25% vs current baseline (based on your June 2026 billing data)
   - Quality: end-to-end extraction and summary accuracy >= 95% on your eval set (we'll collaborate on a labeled sample)
   - Reliability: automatic fallback to smaller model variant with graceful degradation during degraded capacity

2) Evaluation plan / ownership:
   - FinServCorp: provide sample traffic (anonymized), gold-label eval set (2-3k examples), and a primary engineering contact (Raj).
   - Redwood: provide POC environment (private instance on Dedicated), onboarding document, weekly telemetry reports, and a test harness for automated scoring.

3) Timeline (proposed):
   - Week 0 (this week): Align on success criteria, sign minimal POC MOU, and share eval data sample (anonymized).
   - Week 1: Environment setup & initial model config; we run baseline perf tests.
   - Weeks 2-4: Run evaluation passes, iterate model/config; weekly checkpoints.
   - Week 5: Final evaluation run and economic analysis.
   - Week 6: POC review and decision (go/no-go).

4) Resources & access:
   - Redwood will provide a temporary Dedicated slot and a short-lived service account for uploads.
   - We recommend 1-2 FinServCorp engineers and a product owner to engage weekly.

Next steps:
- If this looks right, can you confirm the engineering contact and whether you’re able to share an initial 500-1,000 example eval sample this week?
- Proposed kickoff: Tue, May 4, 10:00 AM PT — 30 minutes.

Attached: 20270502-finserv-poc-plan.pdf, poc-success-metrics.xlsx

Best,
Dylan Brooks
Enterprise Solutions
Redwood Inference

From: Maya Singh <maya@finservcorp.com>
To: Dylan Brooks <dylan@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: Raj Patel <raj.patel@finservcorp.com>
Date: 2027-05-03T08:15:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Demo recap + proposed POC plan — FinServCorp

Thanks Dylan — really helpful recap and the POC plan looks aligned with what we discussed. A few quick questions before we confirm kickoff: 

1) Success criteria — the accuracy metric makes sense, but can you say more on how you’ll measure extraction accuracy vs. summary quality? Will Redwood support our in-house evaluation scripts or do we need to adapt to your test harness?

2) Data handling — we can anonymize the eval samples, but we need to understand Redwood’s temporary storage/retention policy during the POC and whether we can use our KMS for keys.

3) SSO / access — for the Dedicated slot, does Redwood support SSO (SAML/Okta) for our engineers?

4) Timeline — the 6-week plan is fine; can we shorten to 4 weeks if setup goes smoothly? Prefer to keep the kickoff next Tue at 10:00 AM PT if that works for you.

If you can confirm the above and call out any blockers, I’ll loop in procurement if we need an MOU.

—Maya
Head of Product, FinServCorp

From: Dylan Brooks <dylan@redwoodinference.com>
To: Maya Singh <maya@finservcorp.com>
Cc: Raj Patel <raj.patel@finservcorp.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwoodinference.com>, Neha Kapoor <neha_kapoor@redwoodinference.com>
Date: 2027-05-03T09:42:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Demo recap + proposed POC plan — FinServCorp

Hi Maya — great questions, answered below. I also updated the plan (attached) with a brief on measurement and security notes.

1) Measurement approach:
   - Extraction accuracy: we’ll run your gold-label eval set through the extraction model and compute precision/recall/F1 using your scripts. Redwood’s test harness can ingest your evaluation scripts (Docker or Python entrypoint) or we can run them server-side if you prefer.
   - Summary quality: we’ll run ROUGE/L and a small human-blind rating (5-7 examples) with your SMEs for qualitative checks. We’ll sync on the exact scoring notebook during Week 1.

2) Data handling & KMS:
   - Storage: POC artifacts and logs are stored on a temporary bucket with 30-day retention by default; we can shorten retention on request.
   - Keys: We support customer-managed keys (KMS) for Dedicated POCs; Neha (cc’d) will coordinate required config and provide our security checklist.

3) SSO / access:
   - Dedicated POCs support SAML/Okta SSO. For the short POC window we can also provision short-lived service accounts if you prefer not to configure SSO immediately.

4) Timeline flexibility:
   - We can compress to 4 weeks if the eval data and access are provided before or during Week 0 and there are no blocking security approvals.

Next actions I’ll take:
- Marissa will own the technical kickoff and initial environment setup (she’ll send onboarding steps and a runbook).
- Neha will start the security checklist and confirm KMS/retention details.
- I’ll schedule the kickoff for Tue, May 4, 10:00 AM PT — calendar invite to follow.

Maya — can you confirm Raj as the engineering contact and whether your team can share a sample 500-1,000 anonymized examples by EOD Monday?

Thanks,
Dylan
